findings.issue: かけていいかい？ is an informal permission question ('is it okay if I put on…?'). lit_en misreads いい as 'It'd be nice' (desirability) and かい as an agreement tag 'right?', turning the permission request into a suggestion. Contradicts the record's own (correct) expl_en.
findings.current: It'd be nice to put on a little music, right?
findings.suggested: A little, music (obj.), putting on, is (it) okay? (informal question)

findings.issue: かい is an informal yes/no question particle, not the agreement tag ね; 'bom, né?' reads as 'é bom, não é?', losing the permission question ('posso?') that expl_pt correctly describes. Teaches かい = né, which is false.
findings.current: Um pouco, música (obj.), colocando, bom, né?
findings.suggested: Um pouco, música (obj.), colocando, pode/é ok? (pergunta informal)

findings.issue: 休ませてください is a causative + てください permission request ('please let me rest a little'); en renders it as a plain statement of desire, dropping the request act and 少し. Inconsistent with pt and lit_en, which both render the request.
findings.current: I want to take a rest.
findings.suggested: Please let me rest a little.

findings.issue: そうなった is past ('became that way') and ということですね frames the sentence as a confirmation addressed to the listener; en uses a generic present statement and drops the confirmation entirely, mismatching pt ('Então foi ficando assim aos poucos, né.') and lit_en.
findings.suggested: So it became like this little by little, right?

findings.issue: Internal pipeline metadata leaked into the learner-facing explanation: 'coverage' is an internal target-assignment label, meaningless to a learner. A reviewer would delete this sentence.
Same internal pipeline metadata leak as expl_en, with the English enum value 'coverage' quoted inside the pt-BR learner text.
findings.current: O alvo é 'coverage' (revisão geral de N4).

findings.issue: Authoring-pipeline commentary leaked into the learner-facing explanation: learners never saw any 'proposed focus', so opening with it (and 'the target pattern 〜ないと does NOT actually apply') is confusing meta-talk. The grammar content itself is correct and should be kept, reframed.
findings.current: The proposed focus was 〜ないと, but here the ない is part of 〜たこともない
findings.suggested: Here ない belongs to 〜たこともない ('has never even…'); the following と is the quotative と linking the speech to 言った ('said').

findings.issue: Same authoring-meta leak as expl_en ('O foco proposto era…', 'o padrão-alvo NÃO se aplica') in the pt-BR learner text; should be reframed as a plain contrastive note about ない/と.
findings.current: O foco proposto era 〜ないと, mas aqui o ない faz parte de 〜たこともない
findings.suggested: Aqui ない faz parte de 〜たこともない ('nunca nem…'); o と seguinte é o と de citação, ligando a fala a 言った ('disse').
